newsitem.title: BRAZIL: SOCCER-TROUBLE-HIT PERU AND URUGUAY CLASH IN CRUCIAL QUALIFIER.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-TROUBLE-HIT PERU AND URUGUAY CLASH IN CRUCIAL QUALIFIER.

text.p: Controversy-riddled Peru and the hard men from Uruguay clash in a World Cup qualifier on Sunday that neither can afford to lose.

With Peru sixth in the single South American qualifying group and Uruguay immediately below them on goal difference, the losers could find it impossible to bridge the gap on the leaders in the nine-team competition. Four go to the finals.
Peru have been hit by a scandal involving three players, the desertion of their top midfielder and public uncertainty over whether Uruguay-born goalkeeper Julio Balerio should by allowed to play.
Percy Olivares, Roberto Farfan and Manuel Marango were axed from the squad last week after being photographed drinking with female volleyball players when they should have been in the team hotel.
They were later reinstated pending an investigation by a federation which has already seen midfielder Jose del Solar walk out.

Del Solar, who plays his club soccer in Spain, claimed that he was exhausted after years of trying to reconcile national team and club interests. But local media speculated that there were problems between the highly-paid del Solar and the rest of the squad.

Balerio is due to make his debut on Sunday after being granted Peruvian nationality, but his presence has sparked a public debate. In a recent television programme phone-in, 30 percent of callers said he should not be picked.
Uruguay go into the match with coach Juan Ahuntchain making his debut and a warning from FIFA hanging over their heads.

FIFA said that Uruguay would face severe sanctions if there was any repetition of the rough play that earned the side seven yellow cards in last month's 1-0 defeat in Chile. The loss also led to the sacking of coach Hector Nunez.
Venezuela, win-less and bottom of the group, also parade a new coach at home to neighbouring group leaders Colombia, in San Cristobal.

Eduardo Borrero has included nine uncapped players in his squad, leaving out striker Stalin Rivas and foreign-based midfielder Gabriel Miranda. Colombia are missing injured striker Faustino Asprilla, scorer of six goals in six games.
Second-placed Paraguay, away to Bolivia, have spent three weeks in La Paz acclimatising for their game at 3,600 metres above sea level.

FIFA sparked nationwide celebrations in the Andean nation in May when they allowed Bolivia to carry on playing in La Paz. But the fans' enthusiasm has been dampened since Bolivia were held to draws in two of their last three home games.
Argentina can improve on fourth place if they beat neighbours Chile at home. Ecuador, one point ahead, do not play.
Striker Abel Balbo returns to the Argentine side after completing a two-match suspension and is likely to partner Gabriel Batistuta in attack.
